extracted.intended_audience: naturalists, taxonomists, and field zoologists studying freshwater Bryozoa (Phylactolaemata)
extracted.subtask_description: Morphological, anatomical, reproductive, and ecological criteria for identifying and distinguishing genera, species, and varieties of phylactolaemate (freshwater) Bryozoa, with practical keys, examination techniques, and biological notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gizzard structure (Hislopia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The gizzard is 'uniformly lined with a thick chitinous or horny layer which in optical section has the appearance of a pair of ridges' and has 'a ring of long and very powerful cilia round the passage from the gizzard to the stomach.' The cardiac limb of the stomach is obsolete. The spherical part has an outer muscular circular layer and an inner glandular layer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use detailed optical-section anatomy (lining, cilia ring, muscular vs glandular layers, presence/absence of cardiac limb) as diagnostic internal characters for Hislopia and related taxa; note how the tubular part's inner walls consist of non-ciliated columnar cells and the polypide orientation when retracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green cysts in gizzard (diagnostic and life-history evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The spherical part of the gizzard 'invariably contains a number of green cells ... consist of a hard spherical coat or cyst containing green protoplasm' and sometimes external granules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these cysts as evidence of ingested encysted flagellates (allied to Euglena); observe cyst morphology (coat, nucleus, granules) and behavior (kept in motion by cilia, sometimes regurgitated, often persist for days) when diagnosing species and interpreting feeding biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gizzard function and contents dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: The gizzard 'acts as a food-reservoir' where green cysts and minute organisms are retained until required for digestion; contraction periodically forces contents into the stomach and some cysts may be regurgitated or digested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observations of gizzard contractions, presence/absence of cyst regurgitation, and rate of cyst disappearance (in live specimens or lab conditions) as biological characters and to infer feeding strategies and digestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zoarium form (Hislopia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The zoarium 'forms a flat, more or less solid layer and is closely adherent to foreign objects' often covering considerable area with radiating branches; on slender supports it forms narrow, closely compressed masses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use overall colony habit (encrusting flat sheet vs linear series) and relation to substrate as diagnostic characters for intraspecific forms and subspecies; note that 'one zooecium never grows over another' is a consistent colony-level character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooecia external morphology and orifice characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia variable in shape (irregularly oval, triangular, square); orifice 'situated on a slight eminence' and surrounded by 'a strong chitinous rim' (usually square or subquadrate but sometimes circular), sometimes with spines at corners; dorsal surface 'glassy transparency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine orifice position, rim shape, presence/absence and size of corner spines, chitinous margin and adherent membrane, and dorsal surface texture when differentiating species and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polypide tentacle number
rubrics_metrics.description: The polypide has 'from 12 to 20 tentacles, 16 being a common number.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count tentacles when possible — tentacle number is a straightforward morphological metric useful for species-level identification within genera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subspecific and varietal characters (e.g., moniliformis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subspecies moniliformis has 'zooecia almost circular but truncate or concave anteriorly and posteriorly' and forms linear series with few lateral branches; some named varieties differ by constriction of zooecia posteriorly or resemblance to confined phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colony shape, zooecia outline, host/substrate preference, and regional occurrence to delimit subspecies/varieties; compare types and geographic populations before erecting new taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical distribution as taxonomic evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical forms and subspecies have distinct ranges (e.g., 'typical form common in northern India', 'subspecies moniliformis confined to Lower Bengal', varieties occur in China, Cambodia, Siam); forms appear limited to water free from brine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider geographic and habitat limits (fresh vs brackish) as corroborative evidence for distinguishing taxa, but avoid overreliance — compare morphology across localities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductive biology notes (Hislopia)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Calcutta both eggs and spermatozoa 'are produced at all times of the year simultaneously in the same zooecia', eggs vary greatly in size and are set free as eggs which then grow loose in the zooecium; 'nothing is known as regards the development of Hislopia.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record reproductive mode and timing (simultaneous hermaphroditism, egg size, release stage) as important biological characters; note gaps in life-history knowledge when assessing taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order-level diagnostic characters (Phylactolæmata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phylactolæmata polypide 'possesses a leaf-like ciliated organ (the epistome)' arising between mouth and anus; lophophore usually horseshoe-shaped; 'no parietal muscles'; orifice always circular; tentacles webbed at base; 'all the phylactolæmata produce ... statoblasts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence of an epistome, lophophore shape (horseshoe vs circular), absence of parietal muscles, circular orifice, webbed tentacles, and statoblast production to place specimens at the order level and distinguish from ctenostomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitat and fossil record constraints for order
rubrics_metrics.description: Phylactolæmata are 'confined to fresh or slightly brackish water' and fossil record is scant (only one doubtful fossil referred to the order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fresh(er) water habitat as an expectation for searching/identifying phylactolæmates and treat a fossil attribution with caution unless strong characters are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division-level distinction: Plumatellina vs Cristatellina
rubrics_metrics.description: Division I, PLUMATELLINA: 'Ectocyst well developed; zoaria without a special organ of progression; polypides contained in tubes.' Division II, CRISTATELLINA: 'Ectocyst absent except at the base ... modified to form a creeping "sole"; polypides embedded in a common synoecium of reticulate structure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence/absence and form of ectocyst, zoarium progression organ, and whether polypides are in individual tubes or embedded in a common synoecium to separate these two divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal anatomy of Plumatellina (digestive tract and statoblast-bearing funiculus)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Plumatellina 'a short oesophagus leads directly into the stomach ... cardiac portion ... vertical limb ... pyloric part elongated and narrow, intestine short, straight, and ovoid. A single funiculus joins the posterior end of the stomach to the wall of the zooecium, bearing the statoblasts. Sexual organs are often absent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these internal anatomical characters (stomach limb shape, pyloric extension, funiculus bearing statoblasts) when dissecting specimens for family/division-level identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Fredericellidae defining characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Fredericellidæ: 'Zoaria dendritic; zooecia distinctly tubular, with the ectocyst well developed; statoblasts of one kind only, each surrounded by a chitinous ring devoid of air-spaces; polypides with the lophophore circular or oval when expanded.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colony branching pattern, tubular zooecia, ectocyst development, statoblast structure (no air-spaces in ring) and lophophore shape to recognize Fredericellidae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus Fredericella characters and variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Fredericella shows close external resemblance to Plumatella; statoblasts 'do not float and often germinate in the parent zooecium', polypides sometimes regenerate without brown-body formation, zoaria usually attached to solid objects but some species occur at great depths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish Fredericella from similar genera by statoblast buoyancy and germination behavior, fine lophophore shape, and details of zoarial habit; beware shape variability of lophophore (may change when retracted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Plumatellidae defining characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Plumatellidæ: 'Phylactolæmata which have horseshoe-shaped lophophores and a well-developed ectocyst ... Some or all of the statoblasts are provided with a ring of air-spaces (a "swim-ring").'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lophophore horseshoe-shape, ectocyst presence, and statoblast swim-rings containing air-cells to diagnose Plumatellidae and separate from Fredericellidae and other families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subfamily distinctions within Plumatellidae (Plumatellina vs Lophopinæ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subfamily A, PLUMATELLINÆ: 'Zoarium dendritic or linear, firmly fixed to extraneous objects; zooecia tubular, not fused.' Subfamily B, LOPHOPINÆ: 'Zoarium forming a gelatinous mass in which the tubular nature of the zooecia almost disappears, capable to a limited extent of progression along a smooth surface.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use zoarium consistency (dendritic/fixed vs gelatinous/progressive) and degree to which zooecia remain tubular to allocate specimens to Plumatellina or Lophopinæ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key decision characters for Plumatellid genera
rubrics_metrics.description: Key pivots on: (I) 'Statoblasts without marginal processes' vs (II) 'Statoblasts armed with hooked processes'; within these, characters include whether zooecia are cylindrical or embedded in gelatinous investment, presence/absence of stolon, free statoblast shape (oval vs circular), and polypide posture (upright vs recumbent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the key flow strictly: inspect statoblast marginal processes first, then zooecial arrangement (stolonous vs arising from one another), investment (gelatinous vs not), and polypide posture to reach genus-level identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus Plumatella genus-level characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Plumatella: 'Zoarium dendritic, recumbent, erect, or partly recumbent and partly erect; zooecia tubular, not confined in a gelatinous synoecium; the ectocyst usually horny. Statoblasts often of two kinds, free and stationary ... free statoblasts provided with a well-developed ring of air-cells; polypide with less than 65 tentacles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the combination of colony habit, tubular zooecia with horny ectocyst, two-types-of-statoblast presence (free vs fixed), swim-ring structure, and tentacle counts (<65) to diagnose Plumatella species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key species-level diagnostic characters in Plumatella
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal characters include: ectocyst stiffness (capable of wrinkling only near tips vs contractile/swollen), zooecia tip shape when polypide retracted (rounded vs truncated), free statoblast outline and swim-ring proportions, branching pattern (dichotomous/profuse vs sparse lateral), pigmentation of ectocyst, emargination and furrowing of zooecia, L-shaped zooecia, constricted base, surface annulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare multiple colony regions (see precautions below); use these suite characters together (not singly) to separate similar species (e.g., fruticosa, emarginata, javanica, diffusa, allmani, punctata, tanganyikæ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical examination precautions for species separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Precautions: (1) 'If the zoarium appears to be tangled ... the whole mass should be carefully dissected out.' (2) 'Examine as large a part as possible ... preferably with a binocular microscope ... allowance should be made for irregularities and abnormalities.' (3) 'When the statoblasts are being examined, care must be taken that they lie flat ... surface is parallel to ... nose-piece.' (4) 'To see relative proportions of capsule and swim-ring ... statoblast should be rendered transparent' using strong nitric acid applied judiciously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these practical steps when identifying specimens: dissect tangled colonies, examine extensive material, prioritize typical characters over anomalies, orient statoblasts correctly under the microscope, and use chemical clearing to reveal swim-ring proportions (with caution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration and specimen-preparation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The author 'impressed upon the artist the importance of representing what he saw rather than what he thought he ought to see' and deliberately chose specimens 'preserved by the simple methods' likely available to travellers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing figures or plates, prioritize faithful depiction of observed specimens preserved by common field methods rather than idealized forms; this aids field naturalists lacking advanced preservation facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecological and associative characters (Plumatella)
rubrics_metrics.description: Zoaria found attached to stones, bricks, logs, sticks, floating seeds, stems and roots of water-plants, occasionally to mollusc shells; some species 'shun the light', all confined to shallow water; associated fauna include small oligochaete worms, Chironomus larvae, and epibiotic protozoa; sponges can choke colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record substrate, depth, light preference, and associated organisms as ecological characters that may help identify species or understand colony condition and potential interspecific interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeding observations as biological diagnostic notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations (Gravely) that small green flagellates were swallowed and congregated 'in a little pile under the anus', sometimes passed through the alimentary canal apparently unchanged — implying either flagellates pass through unchanged or polyzoon absorbs their stored food material without visibly injuring them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use feeding trials and gut-content observations to infer feeding selectivity and digestive process. Record whether ingested organisms retain structure within rectum (possible translocation or absorptive feeding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast life-history and germination behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Free statoblasts 'are as a rule set free before the cells they contain become differentiated, and float ... before they germinate'; fixed statoblasts usually 'remain fixed ... and germinate in situ'; occasional premature development inside parentzoecium occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing population regeneration and seasonality, document whether statoblasts are free or fixed, floating behavior, timing of germination, and any instances of in-situ germination or premature polypide formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Larval morphology and settlement behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Larva is 'a minute pear-shaped, bladder-like body covered externally with fine vibratile threads (cilia) and having a pore at the narrow end' that at a certain stage contains a polypide; after brief active life it settles on its broad end (adhesive), everts polypide through the pore, and a fresh polyparium forms by budding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use larval shape, ciliation, presence of pore, initial polypide arrangement, and settlement behavior as characters relevant to life-history studies and when tracing developmental stages in culture or field observations.
